title: Negative lead time in balance.json `warnings` wraps to ~2^64 and passes the 'leads > 0' fail-fast
evidence: core/catalog.odin:532-534: `b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_strained_lead_ticks", 0))` / `b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_critical_lead_ticks", 0))` / `b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "pipe_pressure_lead_ticks", 0))`; core/catalog.odin:541-542: `if b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks == 0 || b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks == 0 || b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks == 0 {`; core/catalog.odin:464-466 (the same file's demand loader, the guarded pattern): `// negative JSON value must reject, never wrap to ~2^64 (the` ... `if mult < 1 || st < 0 || dt < 1 || fl < 0 {`; jint (core/catalog.odin:729-730) returns `i32(x)` for a JSON integer unchanged. Verified on the pinned toolchain (dev-2026-08-nightly:902106f): `u64(i32(-1))` == 18446744073709551615, which is != 0, so a JSON `"node_strained_lead_ticks": -1` loads without error.
detail: Spec I/O matrix: 'Catalog validation | amber ≥ red, or a lead ≤ 0 | load aborts with a named error'. A negative lead is ≤ 0 but the u64 cast happens before the `== 0` check, so the fail-fast never fires — the acceptance row is unhandled.
recommended_fix: Mirror the demand loader: parse each lead via jint into an i32, reject `lead < 0` before the u64 cast (e.g. `if fl < 0 { return {"balance.json", "warnings", ...} }`), then cast.

title: Health-ring pulse runs 16× slower than the code's own comments and art-direction §6.1 claim (~0.078/0.156 Hz delivered vs ~1.25/2.5 Hz stated)
evidence: app/render/view.odin:204: `PULSE16 :: [16]f32{0.04, 0.18, 0.38, 0.55, 0.71, 0.84, 0.93, 0.99, 1.0, 0.96, 0.86, 0.71, 0.53, 0.35, 0.18, 0.05}`; view.odin:212: `idx := (tick + u64(node_id) * 5) / u64(step) & 15`; view.odin:338: `step: u32 = 16 // slow amber pulse ~1.25 Hz @ 20 Hz logic`; view.odin:342: `step = 8 // fast critical pulse ~2.5 Hz`; view.odin:208: `// the per-state rate (amber 1 tick/step = 1.25 Hz, red 2 ticks/step = 2.5 Hz`. With idx advancing every `step` ticks, one full 16-entry envelope takes 16×step ticks: amber 16×16=256 ticks = 12.8 s @ 20 Hz = 0.078 Hz; red 16×8=128 ticks = 6.4 s = 0.156 Hz — the claimed 20/step arithmetic is 16× off.
detail: Epic-4 context (art-direction §6.1): 'the ring pulse rate is itself the escalation signal: slow ~1.2 Hz strained, fast ~2.5 Hz critical'. Delivered rate makes the ring a 12.8 s swell — imperceptible as a pulse. Cosmetic (never feeds state) and deterministic, so goldens hold; the 2:1 slow/fast ratio survives.
recommended_fix: Either advance the index per tick scaled by the rate (`idx := ((tick + 5*node_id) * step / 16) & 15` for a 20/step Hz beat) or correct the comments + docs to the delivered 20/(16·step) Hz.

title: balance.json `warnings` node/pipe lead times (600/200/400) have no consumer anywhere in core, app, or harness
evidence: core/catalog.odin:187-190: `// times in ticks (@ logic_hz: strained 30 s = 600, critical 10 s = 200,` / `// pressure 20 s = 400). The UI reads the leads from here for the telegraph;` / `// the serialized warning state carries the LEVELS only (the catalog_hash fold` / `// pins the numbers to the run).`; repo-wide grep of `node_strained_lead_ticks|node_critical_lead_ticks|pipe_pressure_lead_ticks` in *.odin shows only the loader (catalog.odin:532-534), the `== 0` check (catalog.odin:541-542), and test mirrors (catalog_test/determinism_test). The forecast panel countdown comes from the set-piece's own `forecast_lead_ticks` (app/render/forecast.odin:57: `secs := f.countdown_ticks / u64(max(1, cat.balance.logic_hz))`); the strain legend is static text (app/main.odin:538-539).
detail: Spec (Boundaries + code map): 'The UI reads the leads from here for the telegraph' — nothing reads them; node/pipe lead times are validated + folded into catalog_hash but never displayed or used. No crash; dead data + the telegraph carries no reaction-window information.
recommended_fix: Consume the leads where the telegraph promises them (e.g. the strain legend or a node/pipe warning caption rendering '~30s to failure'), or drop the 'the UI reads the leads' claim from the spec/comments until a consumer lands.
